entries.name: Boulder Bank

facts.claim: DOC: an 8 km walk along an internationally renowned natural spit of boulders; unformed track, 2-3 hours one way, expert route; goes from Boulder Bank Drive to 'The Cut'.

Access from Boulder Bank Drive (off Atawhai Drive, SH6) or by boat from Nelson; no fires or camping; dogs prohibited on the western 4 km 15 August to end of February to protect nesting shorebirds (DOC).

The bank is 13 km long, formed of debris from the Mackay Bluffs swept south over 10,000 years; the last 8 km form the spit separating Tasman Bay from Nelson Haven; width 55 m at high tide to 240 m at low tide; the 1862 cast-iron lighthouse stands near the end (DOC).
Wikipedia: managed as a scenic reserve by DOC.

coordinates_check.note: Recommend the Boulder Bank Drive end as the visitor trailhead; if the owner prefers the lighthouse as the landmark, keep -41.25465,173.26518. Exact path start not confirmed against OSM tags.

entries.name: Wharariki Beach
entries.suggested_bio: A beach of dunes, caves and the Archway Islands on the Tasman Sea, where fur seal pups play in the rock pools at low tide.
entries.bio_note: Lint flag is the word 'iconic'; the rewrite drops it.

facts.claim: DOC: 'the most spectacular coastline in the region, with caverns, islands, sand dunes and a long stretch of beach'; 1 km one way, about 20 minutes from the car park at the end of Wharariki Road; stay at least 20 m from the seal pups that play in the beach's pools.
Wikipedia: best known for the four Archway Islands, one beside the beach and others up to about 250 m offshore; a colony of fur seal pups plays in the pools at low tide.
